units: Y. Succ. V, 55ᶜ bot. מפני שהוא סוֹרֵחַ את הנעימה because it (the sound of the organ) intercepts (confounds) the melody of the song; (Arakh. 10ᵇ מערבב)—Esp. (of a rough-edged surface) to catch (cmp. סִכְסֵךְ); to lacerate.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 30:4">Kel. XXX, 4</cite> <he>סוֹרַחַת את היד</he> it (the flask whose mouth is broken off) catches the hand (when you attempt to get the aromatic unguent out).

<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 7:10">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. VII, 10</cite> <he>סוֹרְחִין את הפה</he> the rough edges lacerate the lips (R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 30:3">Kel. XXX, 3</cite> <he>סורקים</he>, read <he>סוֹרְחִים</he>).

<cite ref="Ketubot 61b:3">Keth. 61ᵇ</cite> <he>שפשתן מַסְרִיחַ את הפה</he> the flax (which the spinner moistens with saliva) makes the mouth sore; Y. ib. V, 30ᵃ bot. <he>מַסְרַחַת</he>, v. <cite ref="U01206"><he>שִׁלְבֵּק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Eruvin 54a:18-26">Erub. 54ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 68:11">Ps. LXVIII, 11</cite>) <he>אם אדם משים … שמְסָרֶחֶת ואוכלת וכ׳</he> if one makes himself like a beast of prey which seizes (with its claws) and eats (differ. in comment.), his learning will stay with him, i.e. only he who is plain in his living will become a scholar; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 795">Yalk. Ps. 795</cite>.
